IMM_001.overview: Both articles report on a major surge of migrants attempting to enter the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco, leading the Spanish government to deploy military forces to support police. Officials confirmed that at least nine migrants were found dead after attempting the sea crossing. Both outlets also report that the incident triggered domestic political backlash against Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez as well as criticism from Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani.

shared_claims.claim: The Spanish government announced it would deploy military forces to Ceuta to reinforce security following the arrival of migrants.

support.quote: Spanish military units are being deployed to reinforce police in the city of Ceuta after migrants in Morocco broke through fences, overwhelming the local force.
Madrid said on Thursday it would despatch soldiers to Ceuta to ensure security after hundreds of migrants entered Spain's north African exclave from neighbouring Morocco

shared_claims.claim: Authorities confirmed that nine migrants died while attempting to reach Ceuta.

support.quote: Nine people were found dead, local authorities said, adding to a toll of 60 migrants who have died attempting to cross into Ceuta in recent months.
The Spanish government's delegation in the enclave told AFP that the bodies of nine migrants who died while trying to reach Ceuta by swimming had been recovered.

shared_claims.claim: Spanish conservative opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo stated that the situation in Ceuta constitutes a national security crisis.

support.quote: The government cannot look the other way... because we are facing a national security crisis.
"The government cannot look the other way regarding its duties because we are facing a national security crisis," alleged opposition Popular Party leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo

shared_claims.claim: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani criticized Spain's migration policy on X following the events in Ceuta.

support.quote: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on X that the images from Ceuta showed that Mr Sanchez's migration policy was "misguided".
"The images coming from Ceuta show how the Madrid government's decision to grant Spanish, and therefore European, citizenship to over 500,000 irregular immigrants is profoundly wrong

shared_claims.claim: Ceuta and Melilla share Europe's only land borders with Africa.

support.quote: Ceuta and Melilla — another Spanish autonomous city located in North Africa — have the European Union's only land borders with Africa.
Ceuta and Melilla have Europe's only two land borders with Africa.

single_source_claims.claim: Spain's Interior Ministry estimated that over 40,000 people swam, leaving 18 declared dead from the process.
single_source_claims.quote: Spain's interior ministry estimates more than 40,000 people swam, with 18 people declared dead from the process.

single_source_claims.claim: Spain's Supreme Court recently ruled that migrants intercepted at sea cannot be summarily returned under the border rejection regime.
single_source_claims.quote: Earlier this month, Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants intercepted at sea while attempting to reach Ceuta or Melilla could not be summarily returned

single_source_claims.claim: Some local business owners in Ceuta were shuttering shops and organising self-defence.
single_source_claims.quote: Enrique Serrano, who runs a women's clothing store in central Ceuta, said business owners were organising self-defence because they believed police resources would be insufficient.

single_source_claims.claim: Spain summoned the Italian ambassador to Madrid following Italy's calls to suspend Spain from the Schengen zone.
single_source_claims.quote: Italy called on Thursday for Spain to be suspended from Europe's open-borders Schengen zone, prompting a backlash from Spain, which summoned the Italian envoy to Madrid.

single_source_claims.claim: Spanish Foreign Minister José Luis Albares accused Tajani of weaponising immigration for partisan demagoguery.
single_source_claims.quote: Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Luis Albares responded by accusing Tajani of weaponising immigration for political ends; He said such remarks were "improper"

single_source_claims.claim: Ceuta leader Juan Vivas said 1,500 migrants had arrived by sea in recent days and that there was no more room.
single_source_claims.quote: The Spanish leader of Ceuta, Juan Vivas, said on Wednesday that 1,500 migrants had come to the enclave by sea in the past few days.

framing_differences.description: ART_63F7E2634B51 places emphasis on the legal context within Spain, specifically a recent Supreme Court ruling restricting summary returns at sea, whereas ART_EA32CCA44378 focuses heavily on the diplomatic spat with Italy over suspending Spain from the Schengen area.

support.quote: Spain's government said it was the "exploitation by mafias and criminal organisations" of this ruling that had triggered the migrant surge
Italy said on Thursday Spain should be suspended from the Schengen zone -- a system of open borders spanning 29 European countries

framing_differences.description: ART_63F7E2634B51 includes perspectives from local business owners, a police union representative, and an NGO director, whereas ART_EA32CCA44378 highlights foreign minister statements from both Italy and Spain.

support.quote: Rachid Sbihi, who leads a local workers association representing Civil Guard officers, said some migrants drowned in the crossing
Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Luis Albares responded by accusing Tajani of weaponising immigration for political ends
